summary.one_liner: ChatArena is a Python library of multi-agent language game environments for studying autonomous LLM agents and their social interactions; the README says it was deprecated on Aug 11, 2025.
summary.what_it_does: ChatArena provides a framework for defining players, environments, and the interactions between them, based on a Markov Decision Process abstraction. It includes several language game environments: NLP Classroom (a 3-player conversation game), Rock-paper-scissors and Tic-tac-toe with an LLM moderator, the social deduction game Chameleon, and PettingZoo-based Chess and Tic-tac-toe environments driven by hard-coded rules. An Arena class runs the main loop and offers a Web UI (via gradio) and a CLI, and games can be loaded from JSON config files. Language backends supply the LLM intelligence, with OpenAI models usable when an API key is set. The README describes how to define custom environments by extending the Environment class.
use_cases: benchmarking LLM agents in multi-agent games
prompt engineering agents for game scenarios
studying social interaction between LLM agents
running the Chameleon social deduction game with LLMs
building a custom language game environment
running a demo web UI for agent conversations
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd chatarena
notable: Multi-agent language game environments built on a Markov Decision Process abstraction
Chameleon social deduction game with clue, accusation, and guess stages
Web UI and CLI for prompt engineering and running agents
Config-file loading of games via Arena.from_config
Guide for porting existing environments, using PettingZooChess as an example
caveats: The README states the project is deprecated as of Aug 11, 2025 and will receive no further updates or support.
OpenAI API key is needed for GPT-based agents; other backends require optional extra installs.
The README's Python requirement is written as 'Python >= 3. 7' (formatting appears garbled).
